title: What is known about 1RB0LB_1LC1RE_1LA1LD_0RB1LF_1LA0RC_---1LC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LB_1LC1RE_1LA1LD_0RB1LF_1LA0RC_---1LC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 10,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 with native_decide; the C simulator finds no halt in the first 109 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 49,167 cells have been visited and 35,800 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 2.03×10<sup>19</sup> steps (exact macro run)
claims.text: A macro simulator (blocks of 6 cells, long runs of equal blocks crossed in one go; exact: every macro step is a run of the machine, counted step for step) ran from blank tape to step 20,369,325,558,327,741,845 without a halt. At this block size it gives the same state, head position and tape as the direct simulator after 2,000,015,650 steps. This is a bounded run and says nothing about later steps.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.502).

claims.title: Macro structure (observed)
claims.text: A bouncer over segments of one six-cell periodic word in its different phases (110101, 011101, 101110, 111010, ...); each sweep shifts the segment boundaries, so counts flow from segment to segment while the right end grows.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The decider pipeline of bbchallenge left it open; no proof either way is recorded here yet.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB1LD_1RC1RE_1LA0RA_1RC0LB_0LA1RF_---1RB up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 49,167 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: One word in many phases
html: Almost the whole tape is one periodic word, 110101, read in different phases (011101, 101110, 111010, ...). Short defects cut it into segments. Every sweep of the head moves the defects a little, so one segment loses a copy of the word and its neighbour gains one, and the rightmost segment keeps growing.

This is read off long runs, not yet proved: the next step is to state these patterns as rules, prove them with tools/py/bbtools/symtm.py, and see whether the counters can ever reach the configuration that halts.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.502).
After 109 steps the tape spans 49,167 cells (45 left of the start, 38,381 right), with a density of 1s of 0.728.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.
